take_homes: What I tell the model first shapes everything it says after. My role, my company and my situation should come first, or I get what most people like me would get.
The agent goes easy on its own work, so I check its reports against what I know. I don't take them as a verdict.
I can save what I learn in a rules file and sharpen it round by round, and I could show that to my HR partners as a shared way of working.

monday.move: Rewrite the context of one real people task I give an AI, adding who I am, our company and what good looks like. Then compare it with an earlier generic answer. Separately, ask my DPO and the works council contact what employee data may go into an AI tool.
monday.who: Me, then one HR business partner I show the comparison to
monday.when: Monday afternoon for the comparison, a call to the DPO that week
monday.stop_condition: Stop if the output needs real employee data before the DPO has answered.
monday.blocker: The works council and DPO have not been asked yet, so the weekly people-metrics idea has to wait.

misconception.why: The module never talked about roles or headcount. The context demo and the 'agent grades itself kindly' point were useful, but nothing touched my question about which roles go.

one_line: The Rome and Saimaa demo is the best ten minutes of the day, but the 'notes' are empty filler and nobody said a word about what this means for people.
